overview.description: Alsos is a sophisticated Hungarian trick-taking game blending Jass structure with Tarokk-style announced figures. In the core three-player form one declarer plays against the other two.

history.origins: Alsos emerged in Budapest in the late 19th century and remained popular through the first half of the 20th century.
timeline: 1880s: Developed as a competitive alternative to simpler Jass games.
1930s: Standardized in G.J. Potter's card game manuals.
Mid-20th Century: Reached peak popularity in cafes and clubs across Hungary.
history.evolution: It evolved from Kalaber-style Ace-Ten play by adopting announced figures from Tarokk, adding heavy bidding and kontra depth.
history.cultural: Regarded as one of the most intellectually stimulating games of central Europe, often compared to Bridge in its depth.

setup.players: 3 active players. With 4 players, dealer sits out each hand.
setup.deck: 32 cards (A, K, Over, Under, 10, 9, 8, 7). Usually Hungarian suits (Acorns, Hearts, Leaves, Bells).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards (dealt in batches of 3-3-3). 5 cards remain in the 'Talon' (one face up to propose trump).

rules.objective: As declarer, score more points through tricks, melds, and 'figures' than the highest-scoring opponent.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding**: Players bid to accept the turned-up trump or name a new suit/game (Betli, Klopitzky). 2. **Melding**: Before the first trick, players announce 'sequences' and 'Vannak' (four of a kind). 3. **The Play**: Declarer competes against the two opponents (who cooperate). 4. **Figures**: During play, players may announce 'Ultimo' (winning last trick with trump 7) or 'Volat' (winning all tricks).
keyRules: Trump Rank: Under (Alsos) highest, then 9, A, 10, K, Over, 8, 7.
No-Trump Rank: A, 10, K, Over, Under, 9, 8, 7.
Kontra: Opponents can double the score if they feel the declarer will lose. Declarer can 'Rekontra' to quadruple.

strategy.basic: Track the trump Under and 9 closely; those two cards control many contracts.
strategy.intermediate: When legal, use talon exchange carefully to convert weak cards into suit control before trick play.
strategy.advanced: Ultimo timing is critical: if opponents can force out your trumps early, last-trick plans collapse.
tips: Cooperation is key for opponents: if one partner has a weak hand, they should sacrifice high cards to their partner's tricks to ensure the declarer is outscored.
Betli (losing all tricks) is a high-reward defensive bid if you are dealt a hand with many 7s and 8s.

list.name: Betli
list.description: The declarer must lose every single trick. Worth 5 game points.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Betli uses the same core engine structure; its special win condition and scoring are captured in rules and scoring text rather than separate engine overrides.

list.name: Klopitzky
list.description: A 'no-trump' variation where every player plays for themselves for one hand.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Klopitzky changes scoring and objective but reuses the main engine loop; variation details are described in the rules instead of engine overrides.

difficulty.easy: Doesn't understand meld hierarchies. Fails to cooperate as an opponent.
difficulty.medium: Understands 'Last trick' importance. Bids 'Accept' greedily on low trump hands.
difficulty.hard: Simulates 'Ultimo' probability. Masterfully calculates when to 'Kontra' based on the declarer's probable talon discards.

considerations: AI must support counter-clockwise turn order and 32-card pack hierarchies.
The 'Declarer vs Two' logic requires two AI instances to share a cooperative state without seeing each other's cards.

additional: Traditional Central European Card Game Standards

phases.label: Initial Deal
phases.notes: Deal first 6 cards to each active player and expose trump-indicator/talon cards.

phases.label: Contract Bidding
phases.notes: Players bid for contract and declarer role, including possible no-trump contracts.

phases.label: Final Deal
phases.notes: Deal final 3 cards to each active player.

phases.label: Second Announcements
phases.notes: Final figure and meld declarations around first trick timing.

phases.label: Trick Play
phases.notes: Contract and trump rules determine follow, trumping, and trick winner.

phases.label: Settle Contract
phases.notes: Resolve declarer vs defenders score including figures, kontra levels, and last trick bonus.

ante.reason: Alsós uses contract bidding and figures; no ante.

deal.description: Dealer distributes cards in two stages (6 then 3).

reveal_market.description: Expose trump-indicator and talon reference cards.

buy_market.reason: Trump from talon; no market buy.

buy_stock.reason: Nine cards dealt in two stages; no stock buy.

check.reason: No check action in this game.

declare.description: Announce figures, melds, kontra, and recontra statements.
declare.constraints: Only in announcement windows and according to contract timing.

reveal_hand.reason: Cards played to tricks; no showdown.

award_pot.description: Apply contract outcome and score transfer between declarer and defenders.

play_card.description: Play one card to trick following contract-specific trump and suit rules.
play_card.constraints: Must follow lead/trump obligations of the active contract.

discard.reason: Cards played to tricks; no discard.

pass.description: Pass in bidding or announcement rounds.
pass.constraints: Allowed only in bidding or declaration windows.

bid.description: Bid contract type or suit, including no-trump variants.
bid.constraints: Must overcall current bid or pass.

meld.description: Declare sequences (terc, kvart, kvint, etc.) or vannak (four of a kind) during the first trick; only the best sequence and best vannak score.
meld.constraints: Declared when playing to the first trick; state length for sequences; optional to declare.

meldConfig.initialMeldRequirement: Declared during first trick; only best sequence and best vannak score.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Declarer-vs-defenders trick obligations depend on chosen contract.

edgeCases.text: With four participants, dealer sits out while the other three play the hand.
Kontra/rekontra escalation can multiply stakes and must be tracked per announcement.
Some contracts are no-trump and use non-trump card order and total-point schedule.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 32-card pack (William Tell or similar): eight ranks in each of four suits (ace, king, over, under, ten, nine, eight, seven). No jokers; used for this contract trick-taking game with trump and no-trump modes.
engine.suitDescription: Four suits, usually German or Hungarian: acorns, hearts, leaves, and bells. Each suit has eight cards; follow suit when able. Trump and no-trump contracts use different rank orders for the same cards.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit; order depends on contract. In trump contracts the under (jack) and nine are often the two highest trumps; in no-trump the order differs. Standard 32-card ranking applies within each mode.
engine.dealPattern: Deal 6 each, expose talon cards, then deal final 3 each after first announcement round.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Fixed hand dealt; no draw during play.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards played to tricks; no discard pile.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Standard 32-card pack; no special action or bonus cards.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Trick-taking partnership game; not a shedding game.
notApplicableReasons.patienceConfig: Multiplayer trick-taking; not a patience game.

hero.title: ALSOS
hero.subtitle: The Hungarian Masterpiece
hero.tagline: A high-stakes fusion of Jass and Tarokk from Budapest card culture.

synthesis.shortDescription: One of the most complex and rewarding Central European card games. Battle as the declarer against two cooperating rivals. Use trumps, melds, and 'figures' like Ultimo to claim victory.

prompts.human: Welcome to Alsos. You bid for contract, announce figures, and then play nine tricks counterclockwise. As declarer, you must outscore both defenders.
prompts.ai: Game: Alsos. Type: declarer versus two defenders. Players: 3 active. Pack: 32-card Hungarian/German. Flow: deal, bidding, announcements, deal final cards, trick play, settlement with kontra multipliers.

scoring.description: Total points come from card values, melds, and figures.
scoring.winCondition: The declarer wins only if their total points exceed the points of BOTH opponents. If either opponent beats or ties the declarer, the declarer 'goes down'.

penalties.Going Down: If the declarer loses, the opponents score all the declarer's points as a penalty.

scoring.splitRules: Melds only score for the side with the 'High' meld (longest sequence).

nullReasons.targetScore: Session game with no fixed target; play continues with cumulative scoring.

assumptions: This baseline uses the documented three-player pre-WWII style as primary profile.
openQuestions: Some rank-order details in Betli/Klopitzky vary by source and era.
